goal: Make stablature look and feel best in class at phone and desktop size: polish the screens a design review found awkward, draw rhythm as real notation, lay songs across wide screens, play tab back through a synthesised bass, and attach voice memos to parts.

entries.title: usability polish: capture height, part card overflow, honest labels
entries.description:
Fix six specific problems found in a design review of every screen at phone and desktop size. This entry adds NO new musical capability, NO new event or part fields and NO migration. It changes layout, wording and where controls live.

1. THE CAPTURE SCREEN WASTES HEIGHT. On a Pixel 7 (412x915) about a quarter of the screen sits empty between the header and the staff. The cause is the tab band in src/components/capture/CaptureScreen.tsx (~line 612): `flex min-h-0 flex-1 flex-col-reverse overflow-y-auto`, which anchors one staff line to the bottom, next to the fretboard, and leaves the rest of the band blank whenever the screen is taller than the staff. Use that height for the staff and for the bars around the cursor. When there is room, the band shows more than the cursor's line: earlier bars on lines above it, wrapping at barlines, and later bars too when the cursor is mid-part. TabStaff already has a `wrap` mode that breaks at barlines (src/components/tab/TabStaff.tsx:108, `barRuns`), documented as "Play view only". This entry makes it work in an editing surface for the first time, so everything capture relies on must keep working on wrapped lines: the caret and the insert-after mark, `followTail`, `keepCaretInView`, `revealGroups`, tap-to-select and tap-to-extend selection, the long-press column inspector, the chord row, the group bracket row and the rhythm row. The line holding the cursor stays nearest the fretboard, because during capture the eyes are on the neck. Decide how many lines to show from the height actually available rather than from a breakpoint. Where there is no spare height (375x667 with six strings, a chord row and a bracket), the screen must look exactly as it does today. Spec 007 amended 003 FR-020/SC-009/INV-013 so that four, five and six strings stay in view at 375x667 with a chord row and a bracket row, with swipe as the guarantee for seven strings or shorter screens. That guarantee and its height e2e test must still hold. This applies to desktop capture as well.

2. PART CARDS SHOUT. Every part card on the song page (src/components/app/SongView.tsx, ~lines 372-395) repeats `+ variant`, Edit and a red danger-variant Delete, so a phone screen shows three red Deletes. Commit #16 already made them icon-only on touch. Move them behind one overflow button per card, with an accessible name that names the part, a target of at least 44px, Escape and outside-tap to close, full keyboard reach and correct focus return. Delete must not be red on the card face, and must keep whatever confirmation or undo it has today; do not weaken it. Moving Edit off the card face must not leave the card with no one-tap way into editing its part. If it would, make the part's label or staff that route, and record the call in the spec.

3. 'name this part' READS LIKE A NAME. An unnamed part shows `part.name ?? "name this part"` (SongView.tsx ~line 356) in the same style a real name would have. Make an empty name read as an invitation to act, not as data, in both themes, without relying on colour alone (see the chord-tone lesson in docs/DECISIONS.md).

4. THE BAND LIST SHOWS THE SLUG. src/app/page.tsx:83 prints `band.slug` under each band name. The slug is plumbing. Remove it from the list, or replace it with something a band member cares about that can be read from local data. Slugs stay in data and URLs. The slug-uniqueness defect (spec 007 FU31) is NOT this entry's.

5. A SIGNED-OUT USER IS TOLD 'N unsynced'. TopBar.tsx (~lines 87-98) and the capture header (CaptureScreen.tsx ~line 599) show `{pending} unsynced` to a user who is signed out and so never syncs. That reads like an error. For a signed-out user, say that the work is saved on this device and invite them to sign in, with a link to /sign-in. Fit the short form into the capture header without stealing the title's 8ch floor (DECISIONS.md, usability-pass follow-ups). The wording must be true on a desktop too, so do not hard-code "phone" where the device may not be one. Signed-in pending state keeps a count. The e2e tests that wait for "no `N unsynced` text" (grouping-queued-row.spec.ts) must be updated to match, not deleted.

6. THE CAPTURE STATUS LINE IS HARD TO PARSE. It runs separate facts together as words, as in "adding at the end Dsus4 D G A whole note" (CaptureScreen.tsx ~lines 656-704 together with `statusFor`/`statusShortFor` in src/lib/capture/latches.ts). That is the insert position, the chord symbol, its tones and an armed latch. Give each fact its own visually separate segment (separators, weight, a label where needed) so it can be read at a glance. It must stay one line at `h-(--status-row)` and never wrap. The 007 known case, a chord active with stack armed (F23), is the test. The short forms used while a digit is waiting, the triplet refusal and the 'not a chord I know' case must all still read. Duration words stay words here; entry `rhythm-notation` may later swap in symbols.

VERIFY IN A BROWSER, per docs/DECISIONS.md: at 375x667, 390x844, 412x915 and 1280x800, at actual size, in both light and dark themes. Light has broken before. Remember the two documented traps. If a style change seems to do nothing, run `npm run dev:clean` before debugging. Never express a tier as opacity over a surface token. Record the before and after measurements of the capture band in docs/DECISIONS.md, and amend any earlier spec requirement this changes in place, as spec 007 did (`npm run check:usability-amendments`).

DOES NOT DO, and who picks it up: no stems, flags, beams or note symbols (entry `rhythm-notation`); no change to the song page's or play view's width or how many staves sit side by side (entry `wide-reading-layout`), so wrapping is added to capture only; no audio of any kind beyond the existing click (entry `tab-playback`); no voice memos or microphone (entry `voice-memos`); no change to sync, storage or the wire protocol.
entries.rationale: First because it is the cheapest and carries the least risk: no new data and no new notation. It settles the two surfaces that later entries add to. It puts wrapped staves into capture, so `rhythm-notation` draws stems on a capture staff that already wraps rather than reworking capture twice. It also moves the part card's actions into an overflow, which gives `tab-playback` and `voice-memos` a place for their per-part controls instead of adding a fourth and fifth button to every card. Nothing here depends on the later entries.

entries.title: rhythm drawn as stems, flags and beams under the tab
entries.description:
Replace the letters that stand in for rhythm with real rhythm notation, everywhere a staff is drawn and on the controls that set a duration.

WHAT EXISTS. src/lib/rhythm/durations.ts is the one table of the six durations (w h q 8 16 32). Each has a `mark` that is a letter or number, words and whole-number ticks, with TICKS_PER_BEAT = 360360 so that groups of 3, 5, 7 and 9 land on a tick. TabStaff draws `column.duration?.mark` as 12px text in the rhythm row (src/components/tab/TabStaff.tsx ~line 603, `tab-rhythm`), centred under the note since spec 007. The column inspector's duration row labels its six positions with `d.mark` (src/lib/capture/properties.ts ~line 176). So a reader sees `q q 8 8 8` under the tab, and the duration buttons read `w h q 8 16 32`.

WHAT TO BUILD.
- Under the tab, draw a stem for every column that has a duration, with flags for a lone 8th, 16th or 32nd, and beams joining runs of 8ths and shorter within a beat. Draw half and whole notes in the way tab-with-rhythm conventionally does, and pick one convention that tells all six apart. Beams must never cross a barline, a rest or a group boundary, and must never span a column whose duration is unset. Beat boundaries come from the ticks the notation reader already computes (`readNotation`/`notationColumns` in src/lib/rhythm/notation.ts). There is NO time signature in the model and this entry must not add one. Bars are explicit barline events, and beaming is by beat, not by bar arithmetic.
- Rests (`kind: "rest"`) with a duration get the matching rest symbol.
- Tuplet brackets are included. A counted group (`groupNumber`, `groupKind` from spec 003) gets its bracket and number with the beamed notes. A plain group stays an unnumbered bracket. The group bracket row above the staff (`tupletRow` in ascii.ts and its TabStaff counterpart) already draws these. Decide whether the screen keeps it, moves it under the tab next to the stems, or draws it only when the group has no durations. A number must never be drawn twice for one group. Say which in the spec.
- Compressed columns. A column with `repeat: N` unrolls into N layout columns, and compact density shows it as `7x8`. Its rhythm must read correctly in both densities.
- Alignment. Stems sit on the note's centre, as the 007 marks do. Beams span columns of unequal width, including columns that a chord label widened (`chordRooms` in src/lib/reading/staff.ts), and must stay attached to their stems when the view control switches between frets, note names and intervals, which changes cell widths.
- The inspector's six duration buttons show the note symbol instead of the letter. They keep an accessible name and a title in words ("quarter note"), keep fitting on one line at 375px (measured at 54x44 each in entry 5's check), and keep the touch and fine-pointer floors from spec 007. If entry `usability-polish` left duration words in the capture status line, decide whether a symbol reads better there.
- Draw with inline SVG or CSS in `currentColor` using the theme's text tokens. Do not add a music font from a CDN. This is an offline PWA, and anything fetched has to survive a cold open with no signal. If a self-hosted SMuFL font is chosen instead, it must be licence-compatible with MIT, served same-origin, and covered by public/sw.js's cache rules (read the file's header first). Recommended: SVG paths, no new dependency.

EVERY SURFACE THAT DRAWS A STAFF. That means the capture screen, including the wrapped lines entry `usability-polish` added; the song page; the play view, wrapped and unwrapped; the paste-tab preview (src/components/app/PasteTab.tsx); and print. All in both themes. A part with no durations at all must render exactly as it does today, with no rhythm row and no height cost. This is spec 005's promise that durations are advisory and null is the common case.

THE HEIGHT BUDGET. Stems and beams are taller than a 12px letter. The capture screen's guarantee at 375x667 (four to six strings in view with chord and bracket rows, 007 FR-064, with its e2e height test) must still hold. If the rhythm row has to grow, the height comes from somewhere and is measured and recorded in docs/DECISIONS.md, and any earlier requirement this changes is amended in place.

THE PLAIN-TEXT EXPORT AND THE PARSER ARE UNCHANGED. src/lib/tab/ascii.ts draws no rhythm today and keeps drawing none. src/lib/tab/parse.ts is not touched, so every invariant in specs/004 holds. Rhythm notation is a screen feature.

VERIFY IN A BROWSER at actual size in both themes, at 375x667 and 1280x800, with a greyscale check. Thin 1px beams and flags at phone size are exactly what measures right and reads as mush. Remember the `npm run dev:clean` and no-opacity-over-surface-token traps. Beat-boundary beaming and tuplet spans need unit tests over the notation reader, including a group containing a `repeat` column and a group next to a barline.

DOES NOT DO, and who picks it up: no dotted notes, ties or new duration values, and no new event fields or migration, because the model holds six plain durations and this entry draws them; no standard-notation staff; no full-width or multi-part layout of the song page and play view (entry `wide-reading-layout`); no sound and no playhead (entry `tab-playback`); no voice memos (entry `voice-memos`).
entries.rationale: Second because it changes the height and shape of every staff, and the wide layout that follows has to pack staves of their final height. Packing several bars per line and several parts per row before stems and beams exist would mean re-tuning that packing once they arrive. It comes after `usability-polish` so it draws on capture's wrapped lines once rather than on a single line that is then rebuilt. It does not depend on playback, and playback does not depend on it.

entries.title: full-width reading layout: a whole song on one screen
entries.description:
On desktop and wide tablets, lay staves across the full width so that a whole song fits on one screen on the song page and in the play view, while phones keep a layout that reads well.

WHAT IS THERE TODAY. The song page is capped at `max-w-3xl` (src/components/app/SongView.tsx ~line 94), and each part card's staff uses about a third of its card on a desktop. The play view (src/components/app/PlayView.tsx ~lines 128-151) is `max-w-screen-2xl` but draws an `<ol className="grid gap-4">` with one full-width card per pass, so a song unrolls into a tall column of cards. That is the opposite of the README's thesis that the whole form should fit on one screen instead of unrolling into metres of linear tab. TabStaff's `wrap` mode already breaks a pass at barlines across lines in the play view (TabStaff.tsx ~line 337, `.tab-staff-wrapped`, `.tab-wrapped-body`). Entry `usability-polish` extended it to capture.

WHAT TO BUILD.
- Several bars per line. On wide screens a staff fills its container's width, wrapping at barlines, instead of sitting in a narrow strip.
- Several parts or passes per row. On the song page, part cards flow into columns on wide screens. In the play view, passes flow across the width so the arrangement reads as a grid in reading order. State which order is used, row-major or column-major, and keep it unambiguous with pass labels.
- A concrete fit target, measured and tested. Pick a fixture song (for example four parts and an arrangement of about ten passes, one of them a variant) and a viewport (for example 1280x800 and 1440x900), and assert that the whole song fits without vertical scrolling on both the song page and the play view. Record the figures in docs/DECISIONS.md.
- Layout follows WIDTH, not pointer. Spec 007 made density follow `pointer: fine` and `pointer: coarse`. That stays, and a wide tablet with a coarse pointer gets the wide layout at touch sizing. Phones in portrait keep one column and today's readability. Check 375, 412, 768, 1024 and 1280 wide.
- Repeated passes. Decide in the spec whether identical consecutive passes are drawn once with a pass count (the arrangement already says `A x4`) or drawn each time. Drawing once saves the most room, but only if the reading-position highlight, keyboard stepping between columns and bars, variant marks (spec 006) and `lastRepeatPartId` substitution still land on the right pass. Recommended: draw once where every one of those holds, and record the call.

THINGS THAT MUST KEEP WORKING across the new layout: bar numbers and section labels (spec 007); the note-name and interval view (cells are wider, so lines re-wrap; see DECISIONS.md T120); variant marks; the chord row, group brackets and the rhythm notation from entry `rhythm-notation`; a bar wider than a line (hidden-scrollbar deviation 7 in spec 007); the reading-position column highlight and the keyboard shortcuts on the play view; `print-keep` page breaking and print; the panels and click cluster from 007; and no sideways page scroll at any width.

A KNOWN DEFECT THIS ENTRY OWNS. At 1280 on a short song, the play view's click bar sits directly under the last card in mid-page (DECISIONS.md, usability-pass browser check and follow-ups). Once a whole song fits on one screen, that becomes the normal case, so fix it here. An earlier attempt to pin the bar to the foot of the screen broke INV-024 (`click-double-tap.spec.ts`, `click-bar-fit.spec.ts`), because the running bar grows a help line and the second tap of a double tap lands on whatever moved. Any fix must keep those tests passing unchanged, for example by reserving the running height at rest (research R17).

The ASCII export is unchanged: layout is a screen concern, and src/lib/tab/ascii.ts and layout.ts's column model stay as they are. Capture is not re-laid out here beyond keeping it working if shared wrapped-staff code changes.

VERIFY IN A BROWSER at actual size in both themes at every width listed above, plus print preview. Remember the `npm run dev:clean` and no-opacity-over-surface-token traps. e2e tests that pin play-view geometry (reading-layout.spec.ts INV-016/INV-017, click-bar-* specs) will move. Re-pin them only where the new layout changes the value on purpose, never weaken them, and list each one in DECISIONS.md as spec 007 did.

DOES NOT DO, and who picks it up: no sound, transport, loop, slow-down or playhead driven by playback (entry `tab-playback`; this entry keeps the existing click-driven highlight working); no voice memos (entry `voice-memos`); no change to how rhythm, techniques or groups are drawn (entry `rhythm-notation` owns rhythm); no new data or migration.
entries.rationale: Third because it packs staves whose shape the first two entries settle: capture's wrapping from `usability-polish` and the taller rhythm rows from `rhythm-notation`. It comes before `tab-playback` because the playhead has to follow the final layout, and a playhead built on the current one-card-per-pass play view would be rebuilt when passes start flowing across the width.

entries.title: tab playback through a synthesised bass voice
entries.description:
Play a part, or the whole arrangement, back as sound. Today the only audio is the metronome click from spec 005.

WHAT EXISTS, and what to reuse rather than duplicate. src/lib/rhythm/scheduler.ts is a look-ahead engine (LOOKAHEAD_S 0.75, TOP_UP_MS 25) with stop reasons (tap, left, hidden, audio-lost, fell-behind), a `playhead()` and `due()` for the display. src/lib/rhythm/audio.ts defines the sound port `ClickClock`, whose `schedule(time, level)` can only queue a click, along with a silent clock for devices with no audio. src/lib/rhythm/stream.ts and notation.ts (`readNotation`, `notationColumns`, the group census with `fitFor`) turn drawn passes into ticks. src/components/rhythm/useClick.ts and ClickBar.tsx drive it from the play view's cluster. The column highlight that follows the click comes from useReadingPosition. Playback MUST share this scheduler, so that the click and the notes run on one clock and stay in time with each other. Generalise the sound port so it can queue a pitched note with a length and articulation as well as a click. Do not build a second timing loop. The click's existing behaviour and tests must still pass.

THE VOICE. Synthesise a bass voice with Web Audio, using oscillators, filters and envelopes, or a plucked-string model. No samples, no CDN, nothing fetched: this is an offline PWA, and audio that works on the dev machine but fails silently on a phone in a rehearsal room with no signal is the failure to avoid. If an AudioWorklet module is used, it is a same-origin static file that public/sw.js caches (read its header, and bump VERSION if the strategy needs it). Pitch comes from the part's tuning through src/lib/tunings.ts (`fretToMidi`). String index 0 is the HIGHEST string. A column with several notes sounds them together.

WHAT IT FOLLOWS. It follows tuning, frets, durations and tempo. It also follows techniques where practical, and the spec lists each of the eleven `Technique` values with what it does to the sound or that it is ignored: legato (no re-attack) for hammer-ons and pull-offs, a pitch glide for slides, an LFO for vibrato, a short dark note for palm mute, a percussive thud for dead notes (`x`), longer sustain for let ring, harmonic pitch at the natural-harmonic frets, and so on. A bend has no target pitch in the model (it renders as `b`, not `7b9`), so pick a fixed behaviour or skip it, and say which. `repeat: N` plays N times. Rests are silent. Barlines take no time. Counted groups play in their ratio, using the same arithmetic the click uses.

NULL DURATIONS ARE THE COMMON CASE. Spec 005 made durations advisory, and most captured parts have none. Playback must still play such a part rather than refuse it. Pick a rule, such as an unset column taking the last set duration or else one beat, and show it the way the click shows `Click is a plain beat.` with a reason. Never invent data: the rule applies at playback and writes nothing.

CONTROLS.
- Play a single part. Its card on the song page uses the overflow or card area set up by entry `usability-polish`, and the spec decides whether capture gets a play-part control too, without spending capture's height budget.
- Play the whole arrangement in the play view, following `drawnPasses` exactly as the screen draws it, including variant substitution and bar slices.
- Loop a part.
- Slow down. A speed control scales the song's bpm for this session only and never writes `song.bpm`.
- Click on or off during playback, with the existing count-in.
- A playhead on the staff. The column highlight follows playback through the full-width layout from entry `wide-reading-layout`, scrolls into view, and stays distinct from a selection in both themes.
Fit these into spec 007's collapsible click cluster rather than adding permanent rows, and keep every 007 floor, the double-tap protections (INV-024) and the keyboard shortcuts. Play and stop already exist as keys, so extend them.

PHONE REALITIES, carried over from spec 005. The first tap is the user gesture that starts the AudioContext. A muted or silent-switch device gets the existing hint. Hiding the page, a lock or a call stops playback cleanly through the existing stop reasons. Falling behind stops it rather than smearing the timing. Spec 005 wrote 'no pitched playback' as out of scope for that entry. Record in docs/DECISIONS.md that this entry adds it, and amend 005's note in place.

VERIFY. Write unit tests over the note stream (pitches from tuning, lengths from durations and ratios, technique mapping, the null-duration rule) using the fake clock pattern the scheduler tests already use. Do a browser check at actual size in both themes for the controls and the playhead. Real-phone items for audibility, silent switch and airplane mode from the home screen are owed, and the spec says so.

DOES NOT DO, and who picks it up: no recording, microphone or audio attachments (entry `voice-memos`); no audio or MIDI export; no sampled instruments, drums or other parts' instruments; no per-part tempo and no time signature; no pitch detection; no change to how notation is drawn (entries `rhythm-notation` and `wide-reading-layout`).
entries.rationale: Fourth because its playhead runs over the layout `wide-reading-layout` produces, and its per-part controls go into the card overflow from `usability-polish`. It also benefits from `rhythm-notation` having made durations visible, so a listener can see what is being played. It is the riskiest audio work, so it lands before `voice-memos`. That way the rule for which sound has the device at a given moment is settled before a second kind of audio arrives.

entries.title: voice memos on a part, recorded offline and synced to the band
entries.description:
Let someone at practice record a short audio clip on a part with the phone's microphone, keep it on the device with no network, play it back beside the tab, and sync it to the rest of the band through the server.

THIS IS THE ONLY ENTRY THAT CHANGES SYNC AND STORAGE, and the README's architecture constrains it. Screens read only from IndexedDB through Dexie's `useLiveQuery`, and Postgres is downstream of the local store. Ids are client-minted UUIDv7. Every mergeable field carries its own HLC. Deletes are tombstones. Merging must stay commutative and idempotent; there is a test over all 24 orderings of four edits. src/db/schema/assert-model.ts fails `npm run typecheck` when the SQL schema drifts from src/lib/model.ts, which is a guard, not an obstacle.

THE DESIGN TO FOLLOW. Split metadata from bytes.
- METADATA is an ordinary synced row: a new memo table with an id, the part it belongs to, who recorded it, its length in milliseconds, MIME type, byte size and creation time, plus an optional label and a tombstone. It goes through model.ts and MERGEABLE_FIELDS, a Drizzle table plus a generated migration, assert-model.ts, the wire schema in src/lib/sync/protocol.ts, src/lib/sync/merge.ts, the server's push and pull in src/lib/server/sync.ts, and a new Dexie version in src/lib/local/db.ts. Writes go through the local write path, not raw Dexie inserts, or they will not sync.
- AUDIO BYTES do NOT ride the row sync. A pull returns up to 500 rows (`limit` in protocol.ts), and audio would starve it. Store the blob in IndexedDB under the memo's id. Upload and download it through new authenticated API routes that check band membership (src/lib/server/membership.ts). Uploads are queued while offline and retried when the device is online and signed in. A device that has a memo's row but not its bytes shows that it is still downloading or not yet downloaded, never a broken player. Self-hosting needs only docker-compose.yml and .env (README), so do not add a storage service. Postgres (bytea, or a large-object table) is the recommended store, and the spec says which.
- SIZE LIMITS. Set a maximum clip length, with recording stopping itself at the limit and a visible countdown, and a maximum byte size. The server enforces the byte limit on the stream it reads, not by trusting Content-Length, and refuses with a readable error that the client shows. Allow-list the MIME types. Consider a per-band total and say whether one is set. Ask for persistent storage (`navigator.storage.persist`) and handle a full quota with a readable message rather than a lost clip.
- DELETING a memo tombstones the row as everything else does. Say whether and when the server and other devices drop the bytes.

RECORDING REALITIES.
- Use getUserMedia and MediaRecorder. The recorded format differs by browser: iOS Safari gives audio/mp4 and Chrome gives audio/webm with opus. Store the MIME type, and when a device cannot play a memo's format, say so rather than failing silently.
- getUserMedia REQUIRES A SECURE CONTEXT. The README tells self-hosters to set APP_URL to the address the phone uses, which is often plain http on a LAN IP. There, the microphone does not exist. Detect this and explain it in the UI, and add a note to the README.
- Denied permission, a call that interrupts recording, and the page being hidden mid-recording must each end with the clip either kept up to that point or plainly discarded. Never a silent loss.
- One sound at a time. Recording or playing a memo stops tab playback and the click (entry `tab-playback`) through the shared engine's stop path, or the spec states the intended overlap explicitly.

WHERE IT LIVES. A record control and the part's memos sit beside the tab on the part card. Use the overflow from entry `usability-polish` for record if the card face has no room, and the full-width layout from entry `wide-reading-layout` for the memo list. If memos also appear on the capture screen, they must not spend the capture height budget (007 FR-064 and the height e2e test). A signed-out user can record and play memos locally, and they stay on the device, consistent with the 'saved on this device' wording from entry `usability-polish`.

PRIVACY. A voice recording is personal data. Update src/app/privacy/page.tsx and anything else that lists what is stored, before this ships.

VERIFY. Unit tests cover the memo row's merge across orderings, as the existing convergence test does, and server tests cover the size limit, the MIME allow-list and membership on both routes. An e2e test uses Playwright's fake media device for record, then play, then sync to a second context, plus offline recording that uploads after reconnecting. There is a browser check at actual size in both themes. Real-phone items are owed: iOS and Android recording, cross-platform playback of each other's clips, airplane mode, and the silent switch.

DOES NOT DO: no pitch detection, transcription or turning audio into tab (out of scope for the whole roadmap); no trimming or editing of audio; no memos on songs, bands or individual columns, only on parts; no streaming or live audio; no change to tab playback itself (entry `tab-playback`) or to the plain-text export.
entries.rationale: Last because it is the only entry that needs a migration, new server routes and binary sync, so it carries the most operational risk. Nothing earlier depends on it. Its placement beside the tab uses the card overflow from `usability-polish` and the layout from `wide-reading-layout`, and it must coordinate with the audio rules `tab-playback` sets, so building it earlier would mean revisiting it after each of those landed. It is also the natural place to stop if the roadmap is cut short.

entries.title: wide layout: cards per row follow what the cards hold
entries.description:
Entry `wide-reading-layout` (spec 010) lays a song's cards in a grid on wide screens. The number of cards per row follows the screen width, not what the cards hold. In src/app/globals.css (`.reading-cards`, spec 010 contracts/reading-cards.md), every track is `max(var(--card-floor), min(<one --staff-line for the whole list> + padding, half the width))`. So every card in a song is the same width, and short cards can never go narrower than `--card-floor`.

WHAT THE BROWSER CHECK SAW (docs/DECISIONS.md on the docs/browser-checks branch, 'Browser check: wide-reading-layout', findings 1 and 2):
- A song of twelve one-bar parts at 1280x800 draws three cards a row. Each is about 415px wide around a 100px staff, and the last row falls under the fixed click bar. Five or six a row would fit the whole song on one screen, which is spec 010's own goal (SC-001).
- At 1920, a 16-bar part next to two 2-bar parts gets three equal tracks. The long card wraps into four rows in a third of the width, while the two short cards leave most of theirs empty.

DO: size each card from its own content, so short cards pack several to a row and a long card takes the width it needs. Possible routes are per-card spans on a fine column grid, a flex-wrap row with each card's basis set to its own one-line staff width (the hidden `tab-ruler` already measures this per staff), or a dense grid. Pick one in the plan and say why. Keep everything spec 010 holds: reading order left-to-right then down, with the card numbers in that order (no reordering to fill gaps, so no `grid-auto-flow: dense` unless order is kept); a card never narrower than its longest bar; no sideways scroll; the 768px switch; the narrow layout below 768 unchanged (e2e/wide-narrow-unchanged.spec.ts and both fixtures, narrow-before.json and narrow-before.linux.json); print; both themes; Firefox (e2e/wide-sideways-firefox.spec.ts). Spec 010's fit song must still fit 1280x800 above the click bar, and the `short` song should now fit too.
